answer: An agent economy can stop sybils the way a karst landscape stops flash floods: every identity must carry a single cedar torch whose ember stays lit through a long chain of narrow, independently guarded passages, each one stamped by a different keeper who has no stake in the traveller. Forging a thousand identities is cheap, but keeping a thousand embers alive through a thousand real passages, without any keeper noticing the same hand, costs more attention than any bot farm can afford.
